cluster_summary: Taken together, these reasons portray a model that defaults to salience- and template-based heuristics—classic false-belief scripts, label‑equals‑contents, last‑mentioned item, or literal similes—instead of flexibly tracking the narrative. It repeatedly misidentifies whose perspective is relevant, collapses distinctions between reality and multiple nested belief states, and neglects how agents’ knowledge changes with perception or world constraints, so it often answers from an omniscient or naïve observer rather than the targeted character. Across many items, lingering linguistic and pragmatic ambiguities mean the model’s reality‑tracking, conservative, or literal interpretations are sometimes partially defensible against rubric expectations.
